Maintenance Procedures Information System
Introduction

This document sets out the steps for the annual maintenance of liquid (flooded) batteries. It is considered one of the most important maintenance activities required for batteries of all types, in which all operations are carried out to return the batteries to the optimum operating condition and the required efficiency and to make sure continuously that they are fit for service, as required at the time of their initial installation. The attached forms show how to carry out the major overhaul and measure the efficiency.

The first draft was prepared by Eng. Saad Mahmoud Mohamed Bassiouni, reviewed by Eng. Adel Abdel Qader El-Naggar of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector, Middle Delta Electricity Production Company, approved by Eng. Samir Abdel Galil, General Manager of Inspection and Quality Control, and approved by Accountant Mahmoud Mohamed Soliman, Head of the Financial Planning and Forecasting Sector and Supervisor of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector.
How Batteries Work:

Depending on the type of battery, certain conditions must be observed for the batteries to work with high efficiency: charging must be carried out continuously to make up for losses, and the charger must be suitable for the voltage and current of the batteries. It is also important that the loads suit the design of the batteries, together with the number of operating hours the batteries are required to work.

Batteries are an independent voltage source. The idea of using liquid acid batteries in power stations arose because of the great danger when the supply is interrupted or when problems occur in the electrical networks, and because some auxiliary equipment needs to continue operating, such as the standby oil pumps for the turbines, various cooling equipment, and emergency lighting.

These batteries were therefore manufactured in different types: dry, acid and alkaline batteries, all of which depend on chemical reactions that ultimately form the negative and positive electrodes, which produce a current between the electrodes and a voltage difference.

From this we see that the formation of the electrodes and the discharge of the charges generated by the chemical reactions require something that restores their charge to the batteries and allows them to be reused – which is what we call chargers – so that the batteries can be used many times while preserving their soundness, always making sure they are fit for service and carrying out the maintenance needed to keep them fit.
How to Test Batteries
To test batteries, several main factors must be taken into account, summarised as follows:

rows: Determine the voltage at which the batteries will operate
Determine the important and main loads by power
Determine the number of operating hours at these loads
Determine the type of connection between the batteries, in series, in parallel, or both together
Select a good quality of battery that withstands heavy duty
Select the type of charger so that it suits the voltage and the charging current required
Provide the equipment and tools used to carry out maintenance correctly

sections_target.text: Occupational Safety and Health Precautions
Issue an approved work order, with the maintenance team holding the appropriate Occupational Safety and Health category card.
Smoking is prohibited in the battery room.
No flammable materials, and no smoking, inside the battery room.
Use the appropriate protective clothing.
Disconnect the charger power supply switch.
Disconnect the batteries from the charger.
Make sure no voltage is present at the batteries.
Make sure the battery output switch is disconnected.
Disconnect the outgoing connection terminals from the batteries.
Provide a standby DC source – if necessary.
Take care to mark the positive terminals in red and the negative terminals in blue, in accordance with international standard specifications.

sections_target.text: Procedure to be Carried Out

rows: Make sure the connections are sound and the cable terminals are tightly fastened, exercising great care
Make sure there are no electrical connection terminals entering or leaving the batteries
Make sure the cooling is sound and the air in the battery room is renewed.
Make sure the batteries are clean of dust and waste
Clean the floors of the battery room of any liquids or other materials
Test the operating cards and make sure they are sound.
Test the charger and make sure it works efficiently
Disconnect the copper connection terminals [battery terminals] and clean them with hot water, removing rust (verdigris) from them.
Measure the liquid levels and readjust them by topping the levels up to their original rates
Make sure the negative and positive terminals (posts) are secure for each battery individually
Make sure the plates inside the battery are sound
Test the battery as a power source by applying a small load to make sure the reaction in it is sound
Reconnect the groups in accordance with the original design
Apply grease to the connection terminals (posts) after connecting the copper terminals, to prevent the formation of verdigris
Cover the cables and the connection points of the groups with a suitable insulating cover
Connect the final terminals (incoming and outgoing) of the groups
Grease the final terminals and cover them with a suitable insulating cover
Remove all the equipment and materials used in the previous work
Clean the workplace thoroughly and return the condition to normal correctly

Third: Measuring the efficiency

In preparation for measuring the efficiency of the batteries, the batteries have been adjusted for specific gravity and tested as above in 'First', and the internal resistance has also been determined and confirmed to be suitable. Returning the battery to its original condition as designed, according to the manufacturer's standard specifications, we have the following information: battery voltage, battery current, number of operating hours, and the loads used for the batteries.
Therefore, after confirming the battery voltage and current, the battery is loaded with the required loads and the voltage and current readings are taken according to the following table:
By recording the data in the table, any changes that occur can be written in the remarks column.

From the remarks we find the start of the voltage drop to 85% of the rated voltage, at which we have the number of operating hours; thus we find that the number of operating hours is in good condition, and by comparing it with the number of hours the battery is designed for, the efficiency can be measured.
Since the efficiency law is:
In this case the efficiency is compared with the number of operating hours in good condition divided by the number of operating hours the batteries are designed for, to give the required efficiency.
